help.title: How DropWheel works
help.body:
1. Grab a file with the mouse (in File Explorer, on the desktop, an image in your browser, an Outlook attachment…).
2. While dragging, tap a key:
     {0} – convert to another format
     {1} – tools (compress, shrink, trim, merge…)
     {2} – actions (copy, move, path, terminal, floating shelf, share)
3. Drop the file on a slice of the wheel. Drop it in the middle to cancel.

The wheel stays open until you drop; you can release the key and tap another one to switch wheels.
Tap the same key again to "repeat the last action".

Without the mouse: select files in File Explorer (or copy a file or a screenshot) and press {3}.
Arrows pick a slice, Enter runs it, Tab switches wheels, Esc closes.
Also via right-click → “DropWheel…”.

The result is saved next to the original file; the original stays untouched.

tool.lock.unlock.removeHint: Removing protection restores the original file or folder in place. The content will no longer be encrypted.
tool.lock.unlock.resetOffer: You opened this file with the Rescuer key. Set a new Rescuer password now?
tool.protect.warn.body: This file (or folder) becomes one encrypted file (.dwenc) in place and cannot be opened without a password. To open it you need one of the following: (1) its own file password. (2) The Rescuer password: one password that opens all your protected files. (3) The Rescuer key: the Rescuer recovery key, shown once, used if you forget the Rescuer password. If you lose the file password, the Rescuer password and the key all at once, the file can never be recovered, and nobody can help you, not even DropWheel. Keep the key somewhere safe outside this device.
